claims.statement: The claimed search bounds are: x in [3,8]; y-intervals [7,18] for x=3, [5,12] for x=4, [5,10] for x=5, [6,9] for x=6, [7,8] for x=7, {8} for x=8; and z constrained by max(y, floor(1/R)+1) <= z <= floor(2/R) where R is the residual 1/2 - 1/x - 1/y.

The lower bound x >= 3 is derived from 1/2 = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z + 1/w <= 4/x, so x <= 8; since 1/x < 1/2 for x >= 3, the smaller terms make x = 1 or 2 impossible because they would force 1/x >= 1/2. This is a standard derivation, but the dossier provides no evidence that this derivation was performed or accepted.
The upper bound x <= 8 follows from 4/x >= 1/2 because each reciprocal is at most 1/x; hence x <= 8. Again, this is mathematically routine but not evidenced in the dossier.

For each claimed interval endpoint, concrete integer witnesses just inside and just outside the interval exist and satisfy or violate the original equation, respectively; these witnesses would be required by the acceptance condition but are not supplied in the dossier.

The claimed y-intervals are tight: for each x in {3,...,8}, the interval is the exact set of possible y values, and each endpoint is achieved or refuted by an explicit construction. This remains unverified from the dossier.

The claimed z-interval uses 1/R, but R is not defined in the dossier; it is assumed to be 1/2 - 1/x - 1/y only by context.
